deep dive S66 · plate 66 of 66 · CLOSE — Make the agent earn done

Done is a verdict the worker never casts.

The closing plate reprises the receipt gate with every artifact named — the whole book compressed into a single crossing from unverified words on the left to accepted proof on the right.

Read it left to right. A prompt or claim enters in muted gray — unverified, just words. The gold TaskAuthorization/v3 bar crosses the tall ivory PRE post: the human-sealed decision about what may run. The cyan TaskHandoff/v3 bar carries exactly one bounded attempt through the work zone — portable, revision-bound, and constitutionally unable to accept itself. Then the gold AcceptanceRecord/v1 exits the shorter POST post in Proof Gold: independent verification reran the proof and wrote the verdict. The receipt says done only because that entire chain completed.

The five chips are the discipline as verbs: bound, seal, hand off, prove, accept. Notice who performs them: the agent performs neither of the two that decide. Authorization happens before it starts; acceptance happens after it finishes. The worker may propose, execute, retry, and report — the contract decides what was authorized, and the receipt decides what was accepted. Five verbs, two of them reserved for the system around the agent.

The reviewer route on the plate is runnable, not rhetorical: taskspec demo, an example task plan, taskspec plan, make check, then the release audit. And the book stays honest to the last line: at the audited current commit, make check reaches the release-status projection drift from the previous plate — the route is not currently all-green, and the page says so instead of photoshopping the finish line.

That is the final promise. Not that every attempt succeeds — plenty refuse, and a refusal is a receipt too — but that every result becomes inspectable. A good agent can write the patch; a trustworthy system can explain why that exact patch was allowed to become done.

How to read the plate
  • The gray input is the unverified claim — it enters with no authority at all.
  • The two gold bars are the artifacts no agent controls: TaskAuthorization crossing PRE, AcceptanceRecord exiting POST in Proof Gold.
  • The cyan bar is the handoff — one bounded attempt in the work zone; it never accepts itself.
  • The ivory posts are the gates; the receipt reads done only when the chain completes.
The boundary

The promise is inspectability, not guaranteed success. Failures and refusals are receipts too — and at the audited commit the reviewer route itself carries one known drift, named on the plate rather than smoothed over.

accepts resultcanonical POST gateinvokes Task-Spec acceptance
merges target branchnono; prints human route

Tier Cryptographic state Dispatch Acceptance
1current HMAC v3 verifiesunsupervised eligiblenormal POST policy

Reading the contrasts

Every row is a custody claim: who decides, what is canonical, where the verdict comes from. The tier table flattens nothing — dispatch and acceptance policy move with the cryptographic state, and a Tier 3 seal is refused, never debated.

appendix b code specimens · brief §8 · page 1 of 2

Two paths, both runnable.

The everyday path needs no mesh. The mesh path starts only from an already-authorized frontier — and hands the branch back to a human.

01 · the everyday path
the everyday path · taskspec
taskspec init taskspec setup signing taskspec plan --manifest tasks/.plans/change.yaml taskspec batch --plan tasks/.plans/change.yaml taskspec validate tasks/T-leaf.md taskspec dod tasks/T-leaf.md taskspec gate --stamp tasks/T-leaf.md taskspec handoff tasks/T-leaf.md --backend codex --out .taskspec/handoffs/attempt.json # executor works inside the handed-off boundary taskspec accept --handoff .taskspec/handoffs/attempt.json --stamp tasks/T-leaf.md taskspec status T-leaf

A human approves the plan and holds the key — authorization before work; acceptance runs only after the attempt reports back — acceptance after work.

02 · the taskmesh path
the taskmesh path · taskspec mesh
taskspec mesh doctor taskspec mesh frontier --repo . taskspec mesh explain --task T-leaf taskspec mesh start --task T-leaf --adapter codex-native --model <named-model> taskspec mesh get --run <run-id> taskspec mesh accept --run <run-id> --supervised-by <human> --reason <reason> taskspec mesh finish --run <run-id>

Acceptance stays supervised where the tier demands it, and finish prints the human merge route — the mesh never advances the target branch. Specimens 03–04 continue on the next page.

appendix b code specimens · brief §8 · page 2 of 2

Failures are stable. Receipts are structured.

Refusals come from a closed vocabulary, so tooling can diff them. Acceptance comes as a signed record, so anyone can re-check what it binds.

03 · the stable failure family
closed refusal vocabulary · by gate
PRE: INVALID_TASK · DOD_GAPS · TIER_TOO_LOW HANDOFF: HANDOFF_STALE · GRAPH_INVALID · CLOSURE_DRIFT POST: EVAL_FAILED · EVAL_NONDISCRIMINATING · POLICY_TAMPER SCOPE: BLAST_RADIUS · BASE_DIVERGED MESH: MESH_VERSION_MISMATCH · EMPTY_MODEL · STALE_FENCE

A refusal is a receipt too — the attempt parks with context instead of vanishing, and the code names the gate that stopped it.

04 · the acceptance receipt
.taskspec/acceptance/ · AcceptanceRecord/v1
{ "contract": "AcceptanceRecord/v1", "task_id": "T-…", "task_revision": "sha256:…", "attempt_id": "uuid", "authorization_ref": "hmac-sha256-v3:…", "accepted_by": "independent-reviewer", "accepted_at": "2026-08-26T00:00:00Z", "record_digest": "sha256:…" }

The verdict binds the attempt, the sealed revision, and the authorization — and accepted_by is the independent reviewer, never the worker that ran the attempt.

appendix d terminology · brief §12 · a reader’s glossary

Say it precisely.

The vocabulary is the policy. These pairs are never interchangeable — the wrong word flattens a distinction this book spent sixty-six plates keeping intact.

Task-Spec

The contract-and-receipt product. It owns scope, the gates, and the verdict.

TaskMesh

The optional local control plane. It coordinates authorized work; it never redefines it.

leaf

An XS/S/M/L task — the only thing that executes.

composition node

XL/XXL. It organizes leaves and writes nothing itself.

authorization

Before work — the human-sealed may run.

acceptance

After work — the independent may close. The two are never both “approval.”

TaskRevision

The sealed authority digest. Mutation breaks authorization.

attempt

One execution: one lease, one worktree, one receipt subject.

derived graph · derived state

Projections only. Markdown and Git remain canonical.

Tier 1 eligible

The seal verifies now — never “cryptographically safe.”

host-signed environment evidence

The structural world, signed by the host — the container does not “prove everything.”

local control plane

Never a “hosted orchestration service.”

human merge route

What finish prints — TaskMesh does not “ship the branch.”

current-main

Implemented at audited HEAD, outside the frozen corridor; roster and README marker drift are labeled, never smoothed over.

research providers

Firecrawl, Tavily, and Exa may inform authoring constraints and risks; they cannot satisfy an acceptance gate.

the closing promise

Inspectable authority and proof — not guaranteed success.
